pop_quiz_song1.question:
What word best completes this line in the poem?
'Through galaxies of stars and _____'

options.text: A. flies
B. skies
C. moo
D. blue

A.text: Rhymes with 'eyes', but doesn't make sense in context.

B.text: Fits the rhyme and the meaning! Also surreal and poetic!

C.text: Rhymes with 'through', but too silly for the line.

D.text: Rhymes with 'through', completely offbeat. Try another choice!

pop_quiz_llm1.question: An AI trained on massive amounts of text can understand what words mean and use that understanding to answer questions, just like a human.

options.text: True
False

true.text: Not quite. While AI can predict words and patterns very well, it doesn't actually understand meaning like humans do.

false.text: Correct! AI doesn't truly understand meaning - it's actually very good at recognizing patterns in text and predicting what words should come next.

pop_quiz_llm2.question: What best describes the role of training data when building an AI?

options.text: A. It helps the AI memorize exact sentences
B. It teaches the AI emotional understanding
C. It feeds the AI examples so it can learn word patterns
D. It teaches the AI to translate spoken language into sound

a.text: Not quite. AI doesn't just memorize sentences - it learns patterns from them.

b.text: No, AI doesn't actually develop emotional understanding from training data.

c.text: Correct! Training data helps the AI learn patterns in how words and phrases are used together.

d.text: No, text training data isn't about sound translation.

pop_quiz_llm3.question:
After reading these phrases:
'The sun is shining.'
'The sun rises in the east.'
'The sun sets beautifully.'

What is the AI most likely to predict after seeing: 'The sun…'

options.text: A. sleeps
B. dances
C. is
D. explodes

a.text: No, 'sleeps' wasn't in any of the training examples.

b.text: No, 'dances' wasn't in any of the training examples.

c.text: Correct! Based on the training examples, 'is' appeared after 'The sun' and is therefore most likely to be predicted.

d.text: No, 'explodes' wasn't in any of the training examples.

pop_quiz_prompt1.question: What makes a prompt more likely to give a useful response from an AI?

options.text: A. Keeping it very short
B. Being vague so the AI can be creative
C. Giving clear, specific instructions
D. Asking multiple unrelated things at once

a.text: Short prompts can be helpful, but not if they leave out important details.

b.text: Vague prompts often lead to vague answers.

c.text: Yes! Clear, specific prompts help the AI understand exactly what you're looking for.

d.text: Too many unrelated requests can confuse the AI.

pop_quiz_prompt2.question: Which of these is the best prompt for writing a travel blog post?

options.text: A. Write about travel.
B. Tell me something interesting.
C. Describe a trip.
D. Write a 3-paragraph blog post about visiting Jaipur, focusing on culture, food, and historical sites.

a.text: That's too vague and won't guide the AI well.

b.text: This prompt doesn't give enough direction or context.

c.text: It's slightly better, but still too general.

d.text: Correct! This prompt is specific and gives the AI clear instructions on content and structure.

pop_quiz_prompt3.question: What should you do if the AI's response isn't quite right the first time?

options.text: A. Give up
B. Keep repeating the same prompt
C. Refine the prompt with more detail or clarity
D. Complain to the AI

a.text: No need to give up! Try adjusting your prompt.

b.text: Repeating the same thing usually leads to the same result.

c.text: Exactly! Improving your prompt is the best way to guide the AI toward a better response.

d.text: That won't help. Instead, focus on giving clearer instructions.

pop_quiz_prompt4.question: Why is it helpful to set a “role” in your prompt, like saying 'You are a teacher…'?

options.text: A. So the AI knows how to behave or what tone to use
B. To make the prompt longer
C. It confuses the AI
D. It's required for the AI to work

a.text: Yes! Giving the AI a role helps it tailor its response to your needs.

b.text: Making the prompt longer isn't helpful unless it adds useful detail.

c.text: Actually, roles help guide the AI—they don't confuse it.

d.text: It's not required, but it definitely improves the results.

pop_quiz_model1.question: Which of the following best describes how a machine learning model differs from a traditional mathematical formula?

options.text: A) A machine learning model is always smaller and easier to interpret than a traditional formula.
B) A machine learning model is a fixed set of rules written by humans.
C) A machine learning model has billions of parameters that are learned from data, not directly written by humans.
D) A machine learning model can only process numbers, whereas traditional formulas can process words and images.

a.text: Machine learning models are often very complex and can be difficult to interpret.

b.text: Unlike traditional formulas, machine learning models learn their rules from data, rather than having them explicitly programmed.

c.text: Correct! Machine learning models, especially large ones, have a vast number of parameters that are adjusted through training on data.

d.text: Machine learning models are highly versatile and can process various types of data, including text, images, and audio.

pop_quiz_model2.question: Why can a machine learning model “inherit” biases from its training data?

options.text: A) Because the model is programmed to ignore all data except for biased examples.
B) Because the model statistically reflects the patterns and flaws present in the data it is trained on.
C) Because the model automatically corrects any errors in the data during training.
D) Because the model only uses data that has been manually selected for fairness.

a.text: Models are not programmed to ignore data; they learn from all data provided.

b.text: Correct! If the training data contains biases, the model will learn and reflect those biases in its outputs.

c.text: Models do not automatically correct errors or biases in the data; careful data preparation and model design are needed to address this.

d.text: Not all training data is manually selected for fairness, and even then, biases can still inadvertently be present.

pop_quiz_model3.question: What is the main purpose of the feedback loop during a model's training process?

options.text: A) To randomly change the model’s parameters and hope for better results.
B) To make predictions, compare them to correct answers, and adjust parameters to reduce errors over time.
C) To permanently lock the model’s parameters after the first round of training.
D) To delete any data that the model gets wrong.

a.text: While parameters are changed, it's not random; it's a calculated adjustment based on error.

b.text: Correct! The feedback loop is essential for iterative improvement, allowing the model to learn from its mistakes and refine its predictions.

c.text: The feedback loop is about continuous adjustment, not locking parameters.

d.text: The feedback loop uses errors to adjust the model, not to delete data.

pop_quiz_thinking1.question: What does an artificial neural network primarily do when processing information?

options.text: A) It thinks and understands like a human brain.
B) It performs millions of mathematical calculations to find patterns and make predictions.
C) It randomly generates answers without using any data.
D) It memorizes every example it has ever seen.

a.text: Neural networks do not think or understand; they calculate using math.

b.text: Correct! Neural networks process information by performing fast, complex calculations to spot patterns and make predictions.

c.text: AI models rely on data and patterns, not random guessing.

d.text: While models learn from examples, they generalize patterns rather than memorizing every detail.

pop_quiz_thinking2.question: How does an AI model like a language model 'learn' to generate text?

options.text: A) By reading and truly understanding every sentence.
B) By finding statistical patterns in huge amounts of text data.
C) By copying and pasting sentences from its training data.
D) By asking humans for the correct answer each time.

a.text: AI models do not understand text; they analyze patterns.

b.text: Correct! Language models learn by identifying statistical patterns in massive datasets.

c.text: AI generates new text based on patterns, not by copying directly.

d.text: AI models learn from data, not by asking humans during generation.

pop_quiz_thinking3.question: What is the main difference between how AI and humans approach problem-solving?

options.text: A) AI uses logic and math, while humans also use intuition and emotion.
B) AI is always aware of the meaning behind its answers.
C) Humans cannot make mistakes, but AI can.
D) AI feels emotions just like humans do.

a.text: Correct! AI relies on logic and math, while humans bring intuition, emotion, and ethical reasoning.

b.text: AI does not have awareness or understanding of meaning.

c.text: Both AI and humans can make mistakes, but for different reasons.
